social_security.summary: Since 2024 Montana starts from federal taxable income, so Social Security is taxed to the same extent it is federally taxable; there is no separate Social Security exclusion.
conditions: Taxpayers 65 or older get a general $5,500 subtraction (inflation adjusted from 2025) that applies to any income

sources.quote: "Montana taxable income" means federal taxable income as determined for federal income tax purposes and adjusted as provided in 15-30-2120 .
Taxable Social Security Income and net operating losses are included in Montana taxable income to the extent that they are included in federal taxable income.

public_pension.summary: Government pensions are taxed as included in federal taxable income; the former partial pension, annuity and IRA deduction was repealed for 2024 and later.
conditions: Taxpayers 65 or older get a general $5,500 subtraction (inflation adjusted from 2025) that applies to any income

sources.quote: for each taxpayer that has attained the age of 65, an additional subtraction of $5,500;
"Montana taxable income" means federal taxable income as determined for federal income tax purposes and adjusted as provided in 15-30-2120 .

Repealed Deductions Several deductions are repealed, including: Unemployment compensation Tip income for certain service industry workers Partial interest income deduction for taxpayers aged 65 or older Partial pension, annuity, and IRA deduction

There is a standard subtraction for taxpayers 65 and older of $5,500. If filing jointly and both spouses are 65 and older, the subtraction is $11,000. This amount will be adjusted annually for inflation beginning with tax year 2025.

private_pension.summary: Private pensions, 401(k) and IRA distributions are taxed as included in federal taxable income; the partial pension, annuity and IRA deduction was repealed for 2024 and later.
conditions: Taxpayers 65 or older get a general $5,500 subtraction (inflation adjusted from 2025) that applies to any income

sources.quote: "Montana taxable income" means federal taxable income as determined for federal income tax purposes and adjusted as provided in 15-30-2120 .

Repealed Deductions Several deductions are repealed, including: Unemployment compensation Tip income for certain service industry workers Partial interest income deduction for taxpayers aged 65 or older Partial pension, annuity, and IRA deduction

military_retirement.summary: Resident military retirees may subtract the lesser of 50% of military retirement pay or their Montana wage, business and farm income, for five consecutive years; survivor benefit recipients may subtract up to 50% without the work requirement.
conditions: Lesser of 50% of military retirement income or Montana-source wage, business and farm income
Must have become a resident after June 30, 2023, or been a resident before retirement pay began
Only for 5 consecutive years after becoming eligible
Military survivor benefits: up to 50%, no work requirement

sources.quote: a portion of military pensions or military retirement income as calculated pursuant to subsection (8) that is received by a retired member of: (A) the armed forces of the United States, as defined in 10 U.S.C. 101;

the subtraction in subsection (3)(n)(i) is equal to the lesser of: (i) the amount of Montana source wage income on the return; or (ii) 50% of the taxpayer's military pension or military retirement income.
may only be claimed for 5 consecutive years after satisfying the provisions of subsection (9)(a);

Montana resident working military retirees may be eligible to exempt a part of their military retirement income from Montana taxable income. The exemption also applies to resident beneficiaries receiving military survivor benefits.
The deduction can only be claimed for five consecutive years after meeting the eligibility requirements.

notes: Montana's 2021 tax simplification (effective tax year 2024) moved the starting point to federal taxable income, repealed the partial pension/annuity/IRA exclusion and the old Social Security calculation, and added a general subtraction for taxpayers 65 and older ($5,500 per person in the statute; indexed for inflation from 2025, so the 2025 figure the Department publishes may be slightly higher). Railroad Retirement Tier I and II benefits remain subtracted. The 2025 Form 2 instructions (PDF) say SB 93 removed the expiration date for the military retirement subtraction; not verified against the index.
